341763.title: Extremality conjecture for irreducibles of uniform matroid monoids
341763.statement: Let $M$ be a matroid of rank $k$ on $n$ elements, and let $d4c9_p(M)$ denote its associated monoid. Write $\operatorname{Irr}(\mathcal{Q}_p(M))$ for the set of irreducibles of this monoid. **Extremality conjecture.** The number of irreducibles of $\mathcal{Q}_p(\operatorname{U}(n,k))$ is an upper bound for the number of irreducibles of $\mathcal{Q}_p(M)$, where $M$ ranges over all matroids of rank $k$ on $n$ elements. The conjecture was checked for all matroids on at most four elements, but remains open in general.

344252.title: Existence conjecture for divisible design Cayley digraphs with prime-power parameters
344252.statement:
Let $n$ be an odd prime power. A **divisible design Cayley digraph** is a Cayley digraph that forms a divisible design with parameters $(v,k,\lambda_1,\lambda_2,m,n)$, where the parameters specify its order, valency, within-class and between-class common-neighbour counts, and the number and size of the classes. **Existence conjecture.** There exists a divisible design Cayley digraph with parameters

$$
(n^2-1,n,0,1,n+1,n-1).
$$

The construction is known in the cases checked by computer, and the conjecture asks whether it exists for every odd prime power $n$.

345814.title: The prime power conjecture for perfect difference sets
345814.statement:
Let $D\subset \mathbb{Z}/m\mathbb{Z}$ be a perfect difference set if every nonzero $a\in\mathbb{Z}/m\mathbb{Z}$ can be written uniquely as the difference of two elements of $D$. A perfect difference set has order $n$ when $m=n^2+n+1$ and $|D|=n+1$. **The prime power conjecture.** An integer $n\geq 2$ is the order of a perfect difference set if and only if $n$ is a prime power.

Singer constructed perfect difference sets of every prime power order, and the conjecture asserts that no other orders occur. It has been verified computationally for all $n$ up to $2$ billion, but remains open in general.

349810.title: Cofactor matroid maximality and the valuation rank formula
349810.statement: For $n$ vertices, let $K_n$ be the complete graph, let $\mathcal C^{d-2}_{d-1}(K_n)$ be the cofactor matroid, and let $\operatorname{val}_{K_{d+2}}$ be the valuation associated with $K_{d+2}$-sequences. **Cofactor matroid conjecture.** For all $d\geq1$, the cofactor matroid $\mathcal C^{d-2}_{d-1}(K_n)$ is the unique maximal $K_{d+2}$-matroid on $K_n$, and $\operatorname{val}_{K_{d+2}}$ is its rank function. The case $d=3$ was recently verified in the cited joint work; the assertion for all $d$ is open.

350630.title: The uberhomology conjecture for trees, complete bipartite graphs and paths
350630.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph, let $K_{m,n}$ be the complete bipartite graph on parts of sizes $m$ and $n$, and let $L_m$ denote the graph used in the paper. Write $\mathbb{H}^0(G)$ for the relevant degree-zero uberhomology and $\mathbb{F}_{(r)}$ for the group appearing in the paper's computations.

**Uberhomology conjecture for trees, complete bipartite graphs and paths.** The following assertions hold in general:

- $\mathbb{H}^0(G)=0$ if $G$ is a tree.
- $\mathbb{H}^0(K_{m,n})\cong\mathbb{F}_{(2)}$ for all $m,n>1$.
- $\mathbb{H}^0(L_m)\cong\mathbb{F}_{(m-2)}$, where the generator is the sum of the two connected components in the colouring $\varepsilon=(0,1,\ldots,1,0,1)$.

The conjecture was verified computationally for graphs with up to $10$ vertices. The first and third assertions had subsequently been proved, while the middle assertion remains unresolved in the supplied text.

358857.title: Keevash–Saks–Sudakov–Verstraëte rainbow Turán conjecture for critical graphs
358857.statement:
Let $r\ge 3$ and let $H$ be an $r$-critical graph with $h$ edges. For a multiset of $k$ graphs on the common vertex set $[n]$, write $\operatorname{ex}_k(n,H)$ for the maximum total number of edges among rainbow $H$-free systems. Let $T_{r-1}(n)$ be the Turán graph and $t_{r-1}(n)=|T_{r-1}(n)|$. Also, $t\mathcal{K}_n$ and $t\overline{\mathcal{K}}_n$ denote multisets consisting of $t$ copies of $K_n$ and $\overline{K}_n$, respectively, while $t\mathcal{T}_{r-1}(n)$ denotes $t$ copies of $T_{r-1}(n)$.

**Keevash–Saks–Sudakov–Verstraëte conjecture.** Suppose $k\ge h$ and $n$ is sufficiently large. Then

$$
\operatorname{ex}_k(n,H)=\max\left\{k\,t_{r-1}(n),(h-1)\binom{n}{2}\right\}.
$$

Moreover, $ (h-1)\mathcal{K}_n\cup(k-h+1)\overline{\mathcal{K}}_n$ and $k\mathcal{T}_{r-1}(n)$ are the only extremal structures when $n$ is sufficiently large.

The conjecture has been confirmed when $r=3$ and when $H=K_r$, but remains open for general $r$-critical graphs.

359316.title: Cohen–Harmse–Morrison–Wright shuffle-group conjecture
359316.statement:
Let $[m]:=\{0,1,\ldots,m-1\}$ for every positive integer $m$. For positive integers $k,n$, let $G_{k,kn}$ be the subgroup of $\operatorname{Sym}([kn])$ generated by the standard shuffle $\sigma$ and the pile permutations $\rho_{\tau}$ for $\tau\in\operatorname{Sym}([k])$, where

$$
(i+jn)^{\sigma}=ki+j\quad\text{for all }i\in[n]\text{ and }j\in[k],
$$

and

$$
(i+jn)^{\rho_{\tau}}=i+j^{\tau}n\quad\text{for all }i\in[n]\text{ and }j\in[k].
$$

**Cohen–Harmse–Morrison–Wright conjecture.** The shuffle group $G_{k,kn}$ contains the alternating group $A_{kn}$ if $k\geq3$, $(k,n)\neq\{4,2^f\}$ for any positive integer $f$, and $n$ is not a power of $k$. This conjecture concerns the classification of shuffle groups; it has been confirmed for several infinite families and follows when $G_{k,kn}$ is $2$-transitive, but remains open in general.

361652.title: The strict first-player disadvantage conjecture for random Chomp
361652.statement: A Chomp board is a finite left-justified configuration of cells, and random play means that each legal move is chosen uniformly at random. Consider a starting configuration with more than one row and more than one column. **Strict first-player disadvantage conjecture.** The player going first will win with probability strictly less than $0.5$. This has been verified for every configuration calculated in the paper, but a proof would require understanding how quickly the winning probabilities approach $1/2$.

362912.title: The lower general position product bound
362912.statement:
Let $G$ and $H$ be graphs, and let $\operatorname{gp}^-(G)$ denote the lower general position number of $G$.

**The lower general position product bound.**

$$
\operatorname{gp}^-(G \operatorname{\,\square\,} H) \geq \min \{ \operatorname{gp}^-(G),\operatorname{gp}^-(H)\}.
$$

This conjectured bound relates the lower general position number of a Cartesian product to those of its factors. It has been verified computationally for all pairs of graphs whose orders are at most six, but remains open in general.

362913.title: The terminal set existence conjecture
362913.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph. A **terminal set** is a set of vertices that is in general position and cannot be enlarged by adding another vertex while remaining in general position.

**Terminal set existence conjecture.** Every graph has a terminal set.

Terminal sets are used in the study of lower general position sets. The claim has been verified computationally for all graphs of order at most eleven, but remains open for arbitrary graphs.

364360.title: The rank-4 interlacing-array edge-labeling conjecture
364360.statement:
Let $\operatorname{\mathcal{T}}_{4,n}$ be the set of interlacing triangular arrays of rank $4$ and height $n$, and let $\square_n$ be the $n\times n$ square grid graph. An edge labeling of $\square_n$ uses four labels, and it is face-distinct when the four sides of every face have pairwise distinct labels. **Rank-4 edge-labeling conjecture.** For every $n\geq 0$, $|\operatorname{\mathcal{T}}_{4,n}|$ equals the number of face-distinct edge labelings of $\square_n$.

The conjecture is new in the paper and has been checked through $n=7$; it replaces the refuted rank-4 vertex-coloring conjecture with an edge-labeling enumeration.

366391.title: The strict-partition coloring conjecture
366391.statement:
Let $\alpha=(\alpha_1,\ldots,\alpha_r)\vdash n$ be a partition with distinct parts, where $r\geq 1$. Let $\mathcal{S}_\alpha$ be the set of attainable Robinson–Schensted shapes for cycle type $\alpha$. For a partition $\lambda$, let $\operatorname{SYT}(\lambda)$ denote the standard Young tableaux of shape $\lambda$, call $Q$ admissible when it satisfies the paper’s admissibility condition, and write $Q^\uparrow$ for its associated tableau. An $\alpha$-coloring is a coloring with color multiplicities prescribed by $\alpha$.

**Strict-partition coloring conjecture.** For each $\lambda\in\mathcal{S}_\alpha$, there exists an admissible $Q\in\operatorname{SYT}(\lambda)$ such that $Q^\uparrow$ admits an $\alpha$-coloring.

This conjecture generalizes the coloring result for two-part cycle types and was verified computationally for all $n\leq 13$. It asserts the existence of a suitable colored tableau for every attainable shape, but remains open in general.

366578.title: Kamatchi–Arumugam's distance antimagic conjecture
366578.statement:
Let $G=(V,E)$ be an undirected simple graph. A bijection $h:V(G)\rightarrow\{1,2,\dots,|V(G)|\}$ is a distance antimagic labeling when the vertex weights

$$
\omega(u)=\sum_{v\in N(u)}h(v)
$$

are distinct for all vertices $u$, where $N(u)$ is the neighborhood of $u$. **Kamatchi–Arumugam's conjecture.** The graph $G$ is distance antimagic if and only if no two distinct vertices have identical neighborhoods. The conjecture has been computationally verified for all graphs of order at most $8$, but its general status is not established in the supplied text.

366858.title: Rank-factorization conjecture for the polynomials $P_\lambda(z;q,t)$
366858.statement:
Let $\lambda$ be a partition, and let its **rank** be the size of its Durfee square. Write $P_\lambda(z;q,t)$ for the polynomial associated with $\lambda$. Computations indicate that these polynomials have factors of the form $z+q^it^j$.

**Rank-factorization conjecture.** For any partition $\lambda$ of rank $r$, there is a polynomial $Q_\lambda(z;q,t)\in\mathbb{Z}_{\geq 0}[z,q,t]$ such that

$$
P_\lambda(z;q,t)=Q_\lambda(z;q,t)\prod_{i,j\geq 0\,;\,i+j<r}(z+q^it^j).
$$

Equivalently, $P_\lambda(z;q,t)$ is divisible by each of the displayed linear factors.

The conjecture specifies the linear factors of $P_\lambda(z;q,t)$ in terms of the Durfee-square rank of $\lambda$. It was motivated by computations for small partitions and has been verified for all partitions of size at most $9$; the general statement remains open.

366900.title: Kruft's lower general position number conjecture for Cartesian products
366900.statement:
Let $G$ and $H$ be graphs, let $G\mathbin{\square}H$ denote their Cartesian product, and let $\operatorname{gp}^-(G)$ denote the lower general position number of $G$. **Kruft's conjecture.** For any graphs $G$ and $H$,

$$
\operatorname{gp}^-(G\mathbin{\square}H)\geq\min\{\operatorname{gp}^-(G),\operatorname{gp}^-(H)\}.
$$

The inequality has been verified for all pairs of graphs of order at most six, but remains open in general.

367576.title: Hoàng's degree-sequence conjecture for tough graphs
367576.statement:
Let $G$ be a simple graph. Write $c(G)$ for its number of components, and define its **toughness** by

$$
\tau(G)=\min\left\{\frac{|S|}{c(G-S)}:S\subseteq V(G),\ c(G-S)\ge 2\right\}
$$

when $G$ is not complete, with $\tau(G)=\infty$ otherwise. The graph is $t$-tough if $\tau(G)\ge t$. Let $d_1\le d_2\le\cdots\le d_n$ be the degree sequence of an $n$-vertex graph $G$.

**Hoàng's conjecture.** Let $n\ge 3$ and $t\ge 1$ be integers. If $G$ is $t$-tough and, for every $i<\frac n2$, $d_i\le i$ implies $d_{n-i+t}\ge n-i$, then $G$ is Hamiltonian.

This conjecture is a toughness analogue of Chvátal's degree-sequence theorem. Hoàng proved it for $t\le 3$, Hoàng and Robin proved it for $t=4$, and the source states that it has been confirmed for all $t\ge 4$; thus the conjecture is solved.

369221.title: Foata transform conjecture for spots of unit interval parking functions
369221.statement:
Let $\alpha$ be a unit interval parking function, let $F$ denote the Foata transform, and let $\operatorname{spot}_\alpha$ denote the outcome permutation of $\alpha$. **Foata transform conjecture.** For any unit interval parking function $\alpha$,

$$
\operatorname{spot}_{F(\alpha)}=F(\operatorname{spot}_\alpha).
$$

The conjecture concerns how the Foata transform acts on the outcome of a parking function. It has been verified in the source for all unit interval parking functions of length at most $8$, but remains open in general.

374488.title: Product-of-triangles conjecture for irreducible Ferrers-diagram polytopes
374488.statement: For each integer $d\geq 3$, let $\mathfrak P_d\subseteq\mathbb R^{2d-3}$ be the integral polytope whose integer points correspond to irreducible Ferrers-diagram pairs $(\mathcal D,d)$. A triangle means a 2-simplex. **Product-of-triangles conjecture.** For all $d\geq 3$, the polytope $\mathfrak P_d$ is combinatorially equivalent to the Cartesian product of $d-2$ triangles. This has been verified computationally for $3\leq d\leq 7$, while the assertion for all $d$ remains open.

376113.title: Existence of MDS LCD codes on the maximal hyperelliptic curve
376113.statement:
Let $q$ be a prime power with $q\geq 3$, and let $\mathcal{X}$ be the maximal hyperelliptic curve over $\mathbb{F}_{q^2}$ given by

$$
y^2=x^q+x.
$$

Let $u_B\in\mathbb{F}_{q^2}[x]$ be an irreducible polynomial of degree $q$ satisfying the square condition of Proposition 7 and the MDS criterion of Proposition 6. Let $\mathcal D$ and $G$ be the divisors used in the construction, and let $\mu$ be the multiplier obtained from the square condition. **MDS LCD-code existence conjecture.** There exists such a polynomial $u_B$ for every $q\geq 3$, and the associated code

$$
C=\mu\cdot C_{\mathcal L}(\mathcal D,G)
$$

has parameters $[2q,q,q+1]_{q^2}$. The claim is motivated by a counting heuristic comparing the number of forbidden Jacobian classes with the size of the Jacobian; explicit examples were verified for $q=4,5,7$, while existence for every $q\geq 3$ remains open.

382504.title: The odd-cycle terminating-game nimber conjecture
382504.statement:
Let $C_n$ be the cycle graph on vertices $v_1,\ldots,v_n$, where $n\geq 4$ and each $v_i$ is adjacent to $v_{i+1}$ with indices taken modulo $n$. Let $\operatorname{TER}(C_n)$ denote the terminating geodetic removing game on $C_n$, and let $\operatorname{nim}(\operatorname{TER}(C_n))$ be its nimber. **Odd-cycle terminating-game conjecture.** For cycle graphs with odd $n$, 

$$
\operatorname{nim}(\operatorname{TER}(C_n))=0.
$$

The conjecture concerns the case not covered by the preceding strategy for even cycles; it has been verified computationally up to $n=21$, while the general odd-cycle case remains open.
